newsitem.title: USA: ABN AMRO to keep Citicorp futures staff.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to keep Citicorp futures staff.

text.p: ABN AMRO Chicago Corp will keep nearly all of Citicorp's 150 futures employees, particularly as the Chicago-based investment banking firm expands its overseas futures operations, ABN AMRO Chicago Corp officials said.
"Certainly the vast majority of them will be offered jobs to continue employment with us," James Gary, executive vice president of ABN AMRO Chicago Corp Futures Group, said in an interview.
Gary and other ABN AMRO officials said Citicorp's overseas employees would enhance the firm's plans to open an office in Singapore and to expand its eight-man London operation.
Gary said most of Citicorp's floor employees would be integrated with ABN AMRO Chicago Corp. Citicorp has floor employees at futures exchanges in Chicago, New York, London, Singapore and Tokyo.
"Our interest in Citibank futures was not limited to their existing business, we wanted their people and their infrastructure," Gary said.
On Monday, ABN AMRO said it had agreed to acquire Citicorp's futures business by March 31, pending approval by the U.S. Federal Reserve and several overseas regulators.
A source close to the deal said ABN AMRO paid $20 million for Citicorp's business, which is mostly institutional.
ABN AMRO and Citicorp officials refused to comment on the price or the number of futures accounts on Citicorp's books.
Gary said Citicorp's 25 employees in Singapore and roughly 60 employees in London would be absorbed into ABN AMRO.
"This is a great opportunity to quickly establish the futures operations and quickly grow them, and that's why we did this," he said.
ABN AMRO Chicago Corp has about 1,000 employees in Chicago, 250 in New York and another 250 in its London, Kansas City and Minneapolis offices.
Gary said that once the acquisition was complete nearly 20 percent of ABN AMRO Chicago Corp's staff would be concentrated in the futures markets.

ABN AMRO Chicago Corp, a unit of Netherlands-based ABN AMRO Holding NV, has worldwide responsibility in futures and options business for the entire ABN network. In January, ABN AMRO acquired the Chicago Corporation and merged it with ABN AMRO Securities (USA) Inc.
Citicorp, which is a member of 17 futures exchanges throughout the Americas, Europe and Asia, had been reviewing its strategy in the futures brokerage business since September 1996.
"There were a variety of reasons and we had a variety of criteria in terms of who we would be willing to sell the business to," a Citicorp spokeswoman said.
She said Citicorp would redirect resources to derivatives, foreign exchange, fixed income and emerging markets.

"We felt having our own futures brokering capability was not an essential part to executing our overall strategy based on what our customers want from us," she said. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
